prompt_text: I need a personal injury attorney in Chicago after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
Here are specific Chicago personal-injury law firms to call after a car accident, and why each is worth contacting. I’ve included a mix of large trial firms (for catastrophic or disputed cases) and strong local firms (for more typical crashes).

Top Chicago plaintiff firms to call
- Clifford Law Offices — Well-known for catastrophic auto collisions and wrongful death cases. Deep trial experience, large staff to handle complex cases and investigations. Good to call if you or a loved one suffered severe or life‑changing injuries.

- Corboy & Demetrio LLP — Longstanding Chicago plaintiffs firm with a strong record in auto-accident litigation and high-value verdicts. Known for aggressive litigation and courtroom experience.

- Levin & Perconti — Respected for catastrophic injury and medical-liens experience; they handle complex injury care and damages issues typical in serious automobile crashes.

- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard P.C. — Large trial practice that handles auto collisions and serious personal-injury claims; broad resources and experience negotiating with big insurers.

- Simmons Hanly Conroy — National plaintiffs’ firm with significant resources for major liability fights and complex cases; useful if the crash involves corporate fleets, product defects, or difficult liability issues.

Solid Chicago-area firms for routine to moderately serious cases
- Chuhak & Tecson, P.C. — Chicago-based litigation firm handling personal injury and auto collision cases; strong local court experience and trial-ready.

- D’Ancona & Pflaum LLP — Chicago trial firm experienced in civil and injury litigation; good if you want trial-capable, local counsel.

- Rosenfeld Injury Lawyers (Chicago office) — Handles a high volume of auto-accident cases with a consumer-focused approach; appropriate for many typical crash claims.

Why call several firms
- Different firms specialize in different case types (catastrophic injury, wrongful death, vehicle defects, uninsured/underinsured motorist claims).  
- Big firms provide resources and trial muscle; smaller firms may be more affordable/personal for lower-value claims.  
- Calling 2–3 lets you compare contingency fees, who will actually handle your file, expected timeline, and whether they will advance medical liens/expenses.

What to ask when you call
1. Do you handle car-accident cases like mine? (describe your injuries/circumstances briefly)  
2. Who will handle the day-to-day work — the named attorney or a paralegal?  
3. What is your contingency fee and how are out-of-pocket costs handled?  
4. Do you advance medical bills or liens?  
5. What’s your trial experience for cases like this?  
6. How long do cases like this usually take with your firm?  
7. Can you provide references or examples of similar cases (verdicts/settlements)?  
8. Do you handle uninsured/underinsured motorist claims?  
9. What documents do you need to get started?  
10. Do you offer a free consultation?

Practical next steps
- If you have severe injuries, call a trial firm (Clifford, Corboy, Levin) first. For minor to moderate injuries, a local/consumer firm may be fine.  
- Seek medical care immediately and preserve records and photos.  
- Note Illinois deadlines: personal-injury statutes of limitation are generally limited (often two years for personal injury), so don’t delay contacting counsel — confirm exact deadlines with the attorney.

Want help right now?
- I can draft a short phone script you can use when you call, or help you prioritize which of the above firms to contact first based on your injury severity and circumstances. Which best describes your situation (minor injuries, hospitalization/catastrophic injury, suspected permanent disability, uninsured driver, etc.)?
